title: Stale rollback claims: three code comments say the in-memory driver cannot roll back, and ADR-0067 D3 calls revertCommit atomic
body:
domain:skills#3 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CaqHXh17Qc3C7MRAQw

Filing gate: ① documentation defect with a named producer (two places where written text contradicts the code on `main`), found while reviewing PR #32496 (#32480). ⛔ Not a claim; triage decides lane and grade.

## Item 1 — three code comments say the in-memory driver cannot roll back

On `main`, `packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts` declares `readonly supports = {}` and implements `beginTransaction` (L1265, snapshot of the store) and `rollback` (L1291, restores it). So `driverSupportsTransactions` answers yes and `engineCanRollBack` answers yes for it (PR #32496's amendment and contract review 6812037875 read this; the dev measured it with a one-time probe). These comments still say the opposite:

- `packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts` ~L843, `driverSupportsTransactions` docblock: "A driver with no `beginTransaction` (the in-memory driver, a test double, a foreign engine) has nothing to open."
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts` ~L396, `withTxn` docblock: "Repository code must not rely on rollback for correctness against in-memory drivers."
- `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` ~L5233, `transaction` docblock: "safe to call on drivers without ACID support (e.g. the in-memory driver in tests)".

Fix shape: comments only, no behaviour change.

## Item 2 — ADR-0067 D3 says `revertCommit` is atomic inside one transaction

`docs/adr/0067-commit-history-and-rollback-for-ai-authoring.md` L83 (D3): "`revertCommit(commitId)` — restore every item the commit touched to its pre-commit body, atomically (reuse `restoreVersion` per item inside one transaction)". L18 says the same. On `main`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts` `revertCommit` (L1067) is a per-item loop collecting `reverted[]` and `failed[]`; no `engine.transaction()` is opened in that function. Read from code only; not measured through the public door.

Open for triage: whether this is an ADR amendment (record what the code does) or a code defect (make revert atomic as D3 promises). Either way the text and the code disagree today.

## Reach

Item 1: anyone reading those docblocks to decide whether tests on the in-memory driver exercise rollback. Item 2: anyone reading ADR-0067 to judge whether a failed revert can leave a package half-reverted.

## Duplicate check

Searched open issues for "in-memory rollback driverSupportsTransactions" and "revertCommit atomic": only #32480 (the ADR-0067 D2 amendment, which does not cover D3 or code comments).
